s232_steel.citation: Executive Order 14289 of April 29, 2025 — Addressing Certain Tariffs on Imported Articles
s232_steel.verification_scope: full operative text retrieved and quoted in docs/stacking_legal_model.md
s232_steel.status_note: Sec. 3(a) sets the non-stacking precedence: (i) an article subject to Proc 10908 (autos) is not subject to IEEPA Canada/Mexico or §232 aluminum/steel; (ii) an article subject to IEEPA Canada/Mexico is not subject to §232 aluminum/steel; (iii) §232 aluminum and steel EXPLICITLY stack with each other. Sec. 3(b): exclusion suppresses the rate, not the classification. Sec. 3(c)/4(b): Column 1 HTSUS, §301, EO 14195 fentanyl and AD/CVD remain cumulative. EO 14257 (IEEPA reciprocal) is absent from sec. 2 and is therefore outside the order.

s232_steel.citation: Notice of Implementation of Addressing Certain Tariffs on Imported Articles Pursuant to the President's Executive Order 14289
s232_steel.agency: U.S. Customs and Border Protection / Department of Homeland Security

s232_steel.citation: CBP CSMS #65054270 — Guidance on tariff prioritization for articles subject to more than one action under Executive Order 14289
s232_steel.verification_scope: Bulletin retrieved directly from CBP GovDelivery 2026-07-30. All four load-bearing claims confirmed verbatim against the primary source, not via trade-counsel summaries.
s232_steel.status_note: The >0% definition is the threshold that drives the whole order, and the reason USMCA-qualifying auto parts (0% under Proc 10908) fall through to the §232 steel/aluminum step without a special rule. Note CBP states the USMCA carve-out as a direct exemption from steps 1 and 2; our model reaches the same result from the >0% definition alone, so the two readings agree on outcome and we do not encode a separate USMCA branch.

ieepa_recip_active.citation: CBP: Consolidated Administration and Processing of Entries (CAPE) for IEEPA duty refunds
ieepa_recip_active.status_note: CBP created CAPE in ACE to consolidate IEEPA duty refunds and interest for importers of record who paid them. A CAPE declaration may be filed by the importer of record or the broker that filed the entry summaries (a CSV of up to 9,999 entry numbers); CBP removes the IEEPA Chapter 99 lines, recalculates duties as if IEEPA were never owed, and computes interest under 19 CFR 24.36. Refunds are not automatic and are not guaranteed.

status.headline: IEEPA additional duties have ended
status.summary: IEEPA additional ad valorem duties (the reciprocal action and the fentanyl and border actions) are no longer collected on goods entered or withdrawn for consumption on or after February 24, 2026, under Executive Order 14389 and CBP CSMS #67834313. The IEEPA Chapter 99 numbers became inactive in ACE on that date. This does not affect Section 232 or Section 301 duties. SAIL still shows the IEEPA line for periods when it was lawfully in force and collected.

refund_process.headline: CBP has a streamlined refund path (CAPE)
refund_process.summary: Where IEEPA duties were paid, CBP created Consolidated Administration and Processing of Entries (CAPE) in ACE to consolidate IEEPA duty refunds and interest for importers of record who paid them.
steps: File a CAPE declaration: the importer of record, or the broker that filed the entry summaries, submits a CSV of up to 9,999 entry numbers. CBP validates that each entry exists in ACE and carries at least one IEEPA Chapter 99 number.
CBP removes the IEEPA Chapter 99 lines at the entry-summary-line level, recalculates duties as if IEEPA were never owed, and computes interest under 19 CFR 24.36.
For eligible unliquidated entries, CBP expects to issue valid refunds within roughly 60 to 90 days of accepting the CAPE declaration, unless it needs further review.
Outside CAPE, an unliquidated entry can be corrected by a Post-Summary Correction (PSC), and a liquidated entry can be protested within 180 days under 19 U.S.C. 1514.
refund_process.caveat: CAPE Phase 1 excludes some entries, including reconciliation entries, drawback-related entries, entries with open or suspended protests, certain AD/CVD entries pending liquidation, and entry summaries more than 80 days past liquidation. Refunds are not automatic and are not guaranteed; eligibility and amount depend on liquidation status, timeliness, and documentation.

litigation_risk.headline: Refund scope is subject to active litigation
litigation_risk.summary: The scope of refund relief for certain finally liquidated entries is being litigated, particularly where the importer did not file its own action at the Court of International Trade (CIT).
litigation_risk.implication: Treat refunds on protected entries (unliquidated, timely protested, or covered by the importer's own CIT action) as likely but contingent, and finally liquidated entries with no individual action as at risk.

ui.flag_label: IEEPA duty has ended; a refund may apply
ui.flag_detail: SAIL applied the IEEPA additional duty for this period because it was in force then. Collection ended for entries on or after February 24, 2026 (EO 14389; CBP CSMS #67834313). Where IEEPA duty was paid, a refund may be available through CBP's CAPE process. Refunds are not automatic or guaranteed, and the scope of relief for finally liquidated entries is being litigated.
ui.broker_diff: SAIL shows the IEEPA line for the period it was in force, at the statutory rate. If the broker did not bill IEEPA on a covered entry, that is consistent with an exemption or the post February 24, 2026 wind-down. If the broker did bill it, the duty may be recoverable through CAPE, a PSC, or a protest.
